outcome: psychometric properties of City Birth Trauma Scale (factor structure, internal consistency, known-groups validity, convergent validity)
posttraumatic symptoms after birth (City BiTS scores)
prevalence of PTSD symptoms based on DSM 5 classification
cohort: The study included 437 women aged 18-45 years (mean age 30.5 ± 4.8) who were 6-8 weeks postpartum in Slovakia.
finding: The Slovak version of the City Birth Trauma Scale demonstrated good psychometric properties, comparable to other validation studies, and found 11.5% of postpartum women met the stressor criterion for PTSD, with 2.8% meeting all criteria.
mod_finding: Significantly higher City BiTS scores were observed in women who experienced assisted vaginal birth or emergency caesarian section.
